ex280:
static let machinePreacherCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "pivot", label: "Elbows on the pivots",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.609, y: 0.53),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "pad", label: "Arms on pad",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.741, y: 0.16),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "upper_arm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Wrists straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.318, y: 0.12),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Arms almost straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.391, y: 0.53),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "lower", label: "Lower over two seconds",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.420, y: 0.64),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_R")
        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "pivot",
                title: "Pivot Alignment",
                intro: "Each elbow lines up with the lever's pivot on that side.",
                why: "The lever turns about those two pivots. With the elbows on the same axis, the handle travels the same arc as the hands, so it stays put in the palms from bottom to top; with the elbows off the axis, the handle slides along the hands as it turns.",
                mistake: "The seat set too low, the elbows sitting below the pivots so the handle slides along the palms as it turns.",
                correct: "Before the first set, raise or lower the seat until both elbows sit level with the round pivots at the sides of the pad, then check again with the handle in your hands."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "pad",
                title: "Upper Arm Position",
                intro: "The backs of the upper arms stay on the pad, the armpits over its top edge.",
                why: "With the backs of the upper arms resting on the pad, sloping down at about 45°, the elbows are the only joints that move. Lifting the elbows as the handle rises raises the upper arms, which brings the front of the shoulders into the lift and takes the elbows off the pivots.",
                mistake: "The elbows lifting off the pad as the handle nears the top, the upper arms rising with it.",
                correct: "Keep the elbows heavy on the pad from the first rep to the last and move only the forearms; if the elbows start to lift, take some weight off the stack."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "grip",
                title: "Grip and Wrists",
                intro: "Palms up on the straight handle, wrists straight.",
                why: "In trained lifters, curls with the palms turned up have worked the biceps harder on the way up than palm-in or palm-down curls. Curling the wrists in moves the handle with the wrists instead of the elbows, and a bent wrist grips far more weakly.",
                mistake: "At the top, the wrists bending in so the handle tips back toward the face.",
                correct: "Hold the handle underhand with the hands straight in front of the shoulders and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms from bottom to top."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "range",
                title: "Bottom of the Rep",
                intro: "Each rep starts with the arms almost straight and the plates still lifted.",
                why: "The almost-straight bottom of the curl is the part half reps leave out. In new lifters on preacher curls, training that lower part has built more strength, and at least as much muscle, as training only the upper part, and full-range reps more strength than partial ones.",
                mistake: "Turning each rep back up while the forearms are still angled up, so the plates stop well short of touching down.",
                correct: "Lower until the forearms slope down past level and the arms are almost straight, stopping just before the plates touch down, then curl again without a bounce."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "lower",
                title: "Lowering Speed",
                intro: "Take about two seconds to lower the handle.",
                why: "The lowering half works the elbow flexors too: in training studies, lowering-only work has built about as much muscle as lifting-only work, or a little more. In sets taken to failure, reps lasting from half a second to about eight seconds have built similar muscle, so the aim is control, not a slow count.",
                mistake: "Letting the stack drop, the handle falling back and the arms snapping straight at the bottom.",
                correct: "Curl up in about a second, hold the top for a moment, then take about two seconds to lower without letting the plates touch down."
            )
        ],
        activation: [
            MuscleActivation(name: "Biceps Brachii", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.84),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachialis", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.72),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachioradialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.38),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Forearms", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.30)
        ],
        stabilisers: ["anterior deltoid", "rotator cuff", "core"],
        setup: [
            "Set the seat so your elbows sit level with the pivots on each side.",
            "Sit with your chest to the pad and your armpits over its top edge.",
            "Rest the backs of your upper arms on the pad's slope.",
            "Take the straight handle underhand, hands in front of your shoulders.",
            "Start with your arms almost straight."
        ],
        comparison: FormComparisonCopy(
            correctBadge: "CORRECT FORM",
            mistakeBadge: "LETTING THE STACK DROP",
            correctCue: "Two seconds down, plates lifted",
            mistakeCue: "Handle drops, arms snap straight",
            correctNote: "Lowering under control, about two seconds here, keeps the elbow flexors working through the lowering half, which builds muscle about as well as the lift.",
            mistakeNote: "Letting the stack fall hands the lowering half to the machine and ends each rep with the elbows snapping straight."
        ),
        glows: [
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.06, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.66, cy: 0.31),
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.06, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.49, cy: 0.32),
            .init(DS.activationSoft.opacity(0.30), rx: 0.04, ry: 0.04, cx: 0.59, cy: 0.35)
        ]
    )
